summary: Frontend-only UI smoke test for Wayly Expo on http://localhost:3000 (prod backend via PROD override). Logged in as cathy@example.com and exercised 5 features: Amendments, Visits, Family Wall, Audit Log, Dashboard logo. 4 of 5 features pass end-to-end UI checks. 1 functional regression: the Visits 'When' field is rendered as <input type="text"> instead of <input type="datetime-local"> — the `{ type: 'datetime-local' }` spread on react-native TextInput is silently dropped by react-native-web (which always sets its own type), so the native browser date/time picker is NOT shown on web. Otherwise all hero copy, prefills (For: Dorothy, Your name: Cathy), composer affordances, search input, empty states (Quiet here — for now / Clean slate), and the WaylyHeader logo+wordmark render correctly. Toast errors for empty Generate-letter submission work. Add-another-change appends a row. Family-wall composer renders text input + Photo + Dictate + Post (Post button activates with text). Audit search filters without crashing. Dashboard top-left shows the Wayly mark image + 'Wayly' wordmark.

ui_bugs.issue: The <TextInput> for `starts_at` is rendered as <input type="text"> on web. The `{...({ type: 'datetime-local' } as any)}` spread does NOT override react-native-web TextInput's internal type, so users see a plain text input expecting an ISO-like string ('2026-06-19T20:00') instead of the native datetime picker. Confirmed by reading outerHTML: type="text", no `min`/`step`/`datetime-local` attributes. File: /app/frontend/app/visits/index.tsx:280-292. Suggested fix: on Platform.OS === 'web', render a plain `<input type="datetime-local">` (via createElement or a small web shim) instead of relying on spreading `type` onto TextInput. Alternatives: use react-native-web's `dataSet`/`accessibilityState` to inject the attribute is not sufficient — `type` is owned by TextInput. The cleanest path is a Platform.select that returns a raw HTML input on web.

issues: Dropdown 'For' label renders an unexpected glyph after 'Dorothy' (\uF232 — an Ionicons private-use character) because the chevron-down icon's `numberOfLines=1` truncation appears to swallow the icon into the selectText measurement when the participant name fits exactly. Cosmetic only; the Pictogram still renders as the dropdown arrow next to the text. Worth double-checking on smaller widths.

react_native_issues.issue: family-wall.tsx imports `expo-file-system/legacy`. The legacy entry point is deprecated in expo-file-system v18+; consider migrating to the new top-level API. Reference: /app/frontend/app/family-wall.tsx:31

Console warns 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow.' across screens. Multiple StyleSheet entries still use shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius/shadowOffset. Not introduced in this iteration but worth tracking.
Console warns 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Surfaces during visits modal open and family-wall transitions.

action_items: Fix Visits /visits 'When' field on web: render a real <input type="datetime-local"> via Platform.OS==='web' branch (or a small web-only component) — the current spread of `type` onto react-native TextInput is silently dropped, so users get an unfriendly text input with placeholder '2026-06-12T10:00' instead of the native picker.
Optional polish: replace deprecated `shadow*` style props with `boxShadow`, migrate `props.pointerEvents` to `style.pointerEvents`, and move off `expo-file-system/legacy` in family-wall.tsx.

rca_of_issue: Visits 'When' bug RCA: react-native-web's TextInput component sets `type` internally based on its own props (`keyboardType`, `secureTextEntry`, `inputMode`). External props spread onto TextInput like `{...({ type: 'datetime-local' } as any)}` are forwarded to the underlying <input> as DOM attributes, but TextInput overrides `type` after the spread, so the final rendered element has type=\"text\". Mitigation: render a raw HTML `<input type=\"datetime-local\">` element on Platform.OS === 'web' (e.g., using React.createElement('input', { type: 'datetime-local', ... }) wrapped to mimic TextInput styling), or use a community datetime picker that exposes the native web input.
